title: Fix: the records that come up short
hints: Collect lengths that work and lengths that fail: 4, 10, 130, 200, 300, 500. Write each one as two bytes in hex. What do the failing ones have in common in their **low** byte?

The buffer is `const char *`, and `char` is signed on this platform, so a byte like `0xC8` reads as `-56`. In `p[1] << 8 | p[2]` both bytes are promoted to `int` first; a negative `p[2]` is sign-extended to `0xFFFFFFC8`, and OR-ing that in sets all the high bits. The length comes out as 65480 and the record looks truncated.
Read the length bytes as `unsigned char` before combining them: `(uint16_t)((unsigned char)p[1] << 8 | (unsigned char)p[2])`.
